policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere 6035 (meek) and ketiv 6041 (poor) are near-synonyms of one root. ASV reads 'the poor', and elsewhere it habitually renders 6035 as 'meek', which points to the ketiv; that habit was not verified across the corpus, so it is recorded as suggestive rather than decisive.
The same near-synonymous pair as PSA.9.12 with the readings reversed. ASV again reads 'the poor', here matching the qere, but on the same unverified habit, so it is left undetermined for consistency.
